chapter: Melvin Moore, Hammond and the New York trip
title: Hiring Amos back and his solos on T Town Blues
summary: Hammond wanted the southwest feel, so Fields rehires Amos, whose solos made T Town Blues a hit.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: (Side A of Tape 3 begins at this point.)

--John Hammond wanted, they wanted that feeling, that southwest Texas and Oklahoma feel. They could get readers, guys who could read music and the fancy New York type musicians by the thousands, but that natural, gutsy, soulful feel of the Texas and Oklahoma bands is what he wanted.

That's what I found out, and so anyway, I hired Amos back, put him in there and we left for New York and when we got in we did a couple of sessions and no trouble whatsoever with Amos, and one of the numbers where Amos did solo, he was responsible for the T Town Blues being as big a hit as it was, and if it had really been pushed, I think it would have been a national hit. Amos, frankly, did all of the solo work that we did on all the records; Amos did all the solo work. And if we have a chance before we send them in, see what you think about them.
